etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English arrogaunt, from Old French arrogant, from Latin arrogāns, present active participle of arrogō.

definitions.definition: Having excessive pride in oneself, often with contempt or disrespect for others.

quote.citation: 1878, Friedrich Nietzsche, Wanting to be Loved:
quote.text: The demand to be loved is the greatest of all arrogant presumptions.

quote.citation: 1987, Sam Donaldson, Hold On, Mr President!:
quote.text: Call me a braggart, call me arrogant. People at ABC (and elsewhere) have called me worse. But when you need the job done on deadline, you’ll call me.

quote.citation: 2023 March 8, Howard Johnston, “Was Marples the real railway wrecker?”, in RAIL, number 978, page 53:
quote.text: Transport Minister Marples, meanwhile, used arrogant rhetoric and showed his personal contempt  for railways when confirming in Parliament that a third of the network was to be closed even before the survey results were known.
